title: Impermanence
note: Impermanence is the way that nothing that comes to be can last. Those who say what things are differ in many ways, but all accept this. Attachment doesn’t end until it is understood, so it comes first.

couplets.plain: Having the petty mind that takes what doesn’t last for what lasts is the lowest state.
couplets.pm: The petty understanding that takes passing things to be lasting is a disgrace for those who have renounced. Thinking that what has a beginning has no end, they grow attached to it, and that leads to the suffering of rebirth. Such people cling mostly to wealth and the body, so the next couplets show that these don’t last.

links.quote: takes what doesn’t last for what lasts

couplets.plain: Great wealth comes like the crowd at a dance. It goes the way that crowd goes when the dance is over.
couplets.pm: Great wealth coming to you is like an audience gathering at a stage where dancers perform, and its going is like that crowd leaving when the dance ends. The crowd comes because of the dance and goes when it is over. Wealth comes because of good deeds and goes when they are spent. “Great wealth” includes the wealth of heaven.

links.quote: It goes the way that crowd goes when the dance is over
links.reason: Wealth gathers and scatters as a crowd at a dance does, with nothing to hold it.

couplets.plain: It is the nature of wealth not to stay. When you get it, do at once the things that stay.
couplets.pm: Wealth by nature doesn’t stay. When you get it, do at once the righteous acts it makes possible. Those who have renounced get it only where fate allows, and without fate it won’t stay. These acts are worship of god, giving and the like, done with no thought of reward. They bring wisdom and so release, which is why they are called lasting.

links.quote: It is the nature of wealth not to stay
links.reason: Opens on the plain fact that wealth doesn’t stay.

links.quote: do at once the things that stay
links.reason: The things that stay, which it says to do at once, can only be good deeds, since wealth won’t wait.

couplets.plain: It shows itself as something called a day, but it is a blade sawing through life, if you can find anyone who sees it.
couplets.pm: Time has no parts of its own, yet it shows itself as a measured thing called a day. Life lies at the edge of this blade, which saws without a pause, and what it saws is the body. Those who can’t see this are deceived and enjoy time passing. Those who see it are rare. He rejects the reading that the day itself is the blade, on grammatical grounds.
couplets.note: The plain reading takes the day itself as the blade. He reads it as life lying at the edge of a blade that only looks like a day.

couplets.plain: Before your tongue is stilled and the hiccup rises, rush to do good deeds.
couplets.pm: Before the hiccup rises and stops the tongue from speaking, hurry to do the righteousness that leads to release. It is certain to rise, and once it has you can’t act or even speak. No one knows when it will come, so press forward now.

links.reason: Presses for good deeds now, with the stilled tongue as the deadline.

links.quote: Before your tongue is stilled and the hiccup rises

couplets.plain: This world has this greatness: a man was here yesterday and is gone today.
couplets.pm: This world has so much impermanence that people say of someone, he was born yesterday and is gone today. This is true of women too, but it speaks of men for emphasis. Impermanence is the greatest thing in the world.

links.quote: a man was here yesterday and is gone today
links.reason: With grim irony, names as the world’s greatness that a man here yesterday is gone today.

couplets.plain: They can’t be sure of living one moment more, yet they think thoughts by the ten million, and more.
couplets.pm: The ignorant can’t be sure that body and life will stay joined for even a moment, since your span is only as long as your deeds allow. Yet they think more than ten million thoughts: how to get pleasures and the wealth for them, how to earn it, clear obstacles, guard it, raise friends, ruin enemies and enjoy it all.

links.quote: can’t be sure of living one moment more
they think thoughts by the ten million

couplets.plain: The friendship between body and soul is like a bird that flies off and leaves the egg lying alone.
couplets.pm: It is like the egg left alone when the bird inside flies off in its season. The two begin as one, then part for good. “Friendship” is irony: soul and body are opposites, joined only by deeds. He rejects “nest” for குடம்பை, because a nest isn’t formed with the bird, and the bird goes back into it.
couplets.note: குடம்பை can mean egg or nest. The plain reading follows him.

links.quote: a bird that flies off and leaves the egg lying alone
links.reason: The soul is the bird that flies, and the body the egg left lying alone.

couplets.plain: Death is like falling asleep. Birth is like waking after sleep.
couplets.pm: Death comes as sleep comes, and birth follows as waking follows sleep. As sleeping and waking alternate quickly and naturally, so do death and birth. Birth is named too, to show that impermanence is the one thing that lasts.
couplets.sensitive: likens death to sleep, which a despairing reader may take as comfort

links.quote: Birth is like waking after sleep
links.reason: Each birth is a waking from the sleep of death.

couplets.plain: The soul has been lodging in the body. Has it still found no home of its own?
couplets.pm: The soul has only ever taken shelter in bodies, which are the houses of wind and the other humours. It seems that until now no lasting house has been found for it. It stays while those ailments allow and leaves when they rage, settling in no body. If it had a home it never had to leave, it wouldn’t lodge in others’ houses.

links.quote: Has it still found no home of its own
